promptText: What project management tools exist for a startup founder working solo?
rawText:
As a solo startup founder, your project management needs are unique. You don’t need complex team-delegation features; you need **low friction, high speed, and a way to manage tasks, docs, code/product, and time simultaneously** without spending half your day updating boards.

Here is a breakdown of the best project management tools for solo founders, categorized by how you like to work:

---

### 1. The "All-in-One Workspace" Tools
*Best if you want to combine task management, notes, product docs, and a basic CRM in one place.*

*   **Notion**
    *   **Why it’s great:** It is infinitely customizable. You can build a task board, a wiki, a light CRM for investor outreach, and your product roadmap in a single workspace.
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** Saves money by replacing 3–4 separate apps. Massive library of free templates (e.g., "Startup OS").
    *   **Pricing:** Generous free plan; paid plans start at ~$8/month.
*   **ClickUp**
    *   **Why it’s great:** Extremely feature-rich. It combines tasks, docs, whiteboards, time-tracking, and mind maps.
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** If you want absolute control over your workflows and like having time-tracking built directly into your tasks.
    *   **Pricing:** Free plan available; paid plans start at $7/month. *(Note: Can have a steep learning curve).*

---

### 2. The AI & Time-Blocking Tools
*Best if your main problem is deciding **when** to do work and avoiding burnout.*

*   **Motion (UseMotion)**
    *   **Why it’s great:** Motion uses AI to automatically build your daily schedule. You input your tasks, priorities, and deadlines, and it places them directly onto your calendar around your meetings.
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** Takes the decision fatigue out of "What should I work on next?" If a task takes longer than expected, the AI automatically reshuffles the rest of your week.
    *   **Pricing:** Expensive (~$19–$34/month), but worth it if it saves you hours of planning.
*   **Sunsama**
    *   **Why it’s great:** A daily planner that pulls tasks from your email, Trello, GitHub, or Notion into a unified daily step-by-step plan.
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** Enforces a healthy work pace. It prompts you to plan your day every morning and shut down every evening.
    *   **Pricing:** ~$16/month (14-day free trial).

---

### 3. The Developer & Product-Centric Tools
*Best if you are a technical founder building a software product.*

*   **Linear**
    *   **Why it’s great:** The gold standard for modern tech startups. It is blisteringly fast, keyboard-centric, and beautifully designed.
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** Integrates seamlessly with GitHub/GitLab. You can move tasks from "In Progress" to "Done" automatically just by pushing code. Zero bloat.
    *   **Pricing:** Excellent free tier for up to 250 active issues.
*   **GitHub Projects**
    *   **Why it’s great:** Built right into where your code lives. 
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** Free, zero context-switching if you already spend your day in GitHub.

---

### 4. Simple, Fast, & Minimalist Tools
*Best if you just want to track to-dos without setting up complex systems.*

*   **Todoist**
    *   **Why it’s great:** Quick capture. You can type "Follow up with Stripe on Monday at 9am" and it automatically parses the date and sets the reminder.
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** Lightning-fast mobile and desktop apps. Great for capturing thoughts on the go.
    *   **Pricing:** Free tier is very capable; Pro is ~$4/month.
*   **Trello**
    *   **Why it’s great:** The classic Kanban board (To Do, Doing, Done). 
    *   **Solo Founder Advantage:** Visual, extremely easy to set up in 2 minutes, and completely out of your way.
    *   **Pricing:** Great free plan.

---

### How to Choose (The Solo Founder Matrix)

| If your biggest problem is... | Pick this tool: |
| :--- | :--- |
| **"I have notes, tasks, and ideas scattered everywhere."** | **Notion** |
| **"I spend too much time coding to manage a task board."** | **Linear** |
| **"I struggle with time management and daily focus."** | **Motion** or **Sunsama** |
| **"I get overwhelmed by complex software."** | **Todoist** |

### The Golden Rule for Solo Founders
**Do not spend more than 15 minutes a day managing your project management tool.** 

The biggest trap for solo founders is building elaborate systems in Notion or ClickUp to *feel* productive. Pick the tool with the least amount of friction that keeps you focused on **building, talking to customers, and shipping.**
